newsitem.title: UK: Scotia drops amid further Tarabetic worries.
newsitem.headline: Scotia drops amid further Tarabetic worries.

text.p: Shares in Scotia Holdings Plc plummeted on Friday in further reaction to recent disappointing news on its diabetes drug Tarabetic, dealers and analysts said.
The stock was down 51p at 356-1/2 by 1017 GMT in volume of 179,932 shares -- near its two-year low of 325p set earlier this month in the wake of disappointing news on its diabetes drug Tarabetic.
"This is just a continuation of the issues in terms of credibility because of the Tarabetic news," said Jo Walton, pharmaceutical analyst at Lehman Brothers.

Scotia shares plummeted 23 percent on March 11 after the Medicines Control Agency ruled that it was unable to recommend marketing approval of Tarabetic, though Scotia said the decision was not final and it would ask the Medicines Commission to make a final recommendation.
Walton said the ruling could overshadow the stock for some time to come since it raised questions about Scotia's "lipid" technology.

"This is only one drug but a lot of work is based on the same basic principles," the Lehman analyst said, adding that investors would be looking for fresh news on drug progress at its results next Tuesday.
The company is due next week to make a presentation about its Foscan cancer treatment.
